newsitem.title: CHINA: China names new top officials for oil, Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: China names new top officials for oil, Taiwan.

text.p: China on Tuesday removed Wang Zhaoguo as its top official responsible for dealing with arch-rival Taiwan and appointed his deputy to replace him.
The State Council, or cabinet, gave no reason for the change in an announcement issued by the official Xinhua news agency.
Wang, 55, a protege of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, was replaced as director of the Taiwan Affairs Office under the State Council by deputy director Chen Yunlin, Xinhua said.

Wang, a former governor of eastern Fujian province opposite the island of Taiwan, also heads the Communist Party's United Front Work Department that is responsible for contacts with overseas Chinese and for promoting the unification of China.
The State Council appointed Wang Yonghai and Li Bincai as new deputy directors of the Taiwan Affairs Office, Xinhua said.

The council also removed Wang Tao as head of the China National Petroleum Corp. Wang, who is believed to be close to the official retirement age of 60, was replaced by his deputy, Zhou Yongkang, Xinhua said. It gave no reason for the change.
